OpenAI has used TPUs before. It began renting Google’s AI chips in June 2025, and the report adds that it now owns them. A year earlier, OpenAI said it had “no specific plans to use TPUs at present.” [...] OpenAI has been moving in this direction for a while. It recently said it would offer its frontier models through Google Cloud. In June, it announced its first custom chip, and a current job listing asks for “significant experience optimizing real workloads on TPUs for training or inference.”

A buyer this large wants a second supplier because it gains leverage on price, protection against supply shortages, and software that is not tied to a single vendor. [...] OpenAI has spent more on NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) graphics processors than almost any other company, and it now plans to buy Google’s own AI chips, according to The Information. month.title: OpenAI Is Buying Google’s AI Chips, a Hit to Nvidia’s Biggest Customer Bond - 24/7 Wall St.
month.summary:
No terms, volumes, timing, or chip generation have been disclosed. Until one of the companies confirms it, this remains a reported plan, since nobody has shown a signed order.

OpenAI has used TPUs be...
highlights: No terms, volumes, timing, or chip generation have been disclosed. Until one of the companies confirms it, this remains a reported plan, since nobody has shown a signed order.

OpenAI has used TPUs before. It began renting Google’s AI chips in June 2025, and the report adds that it now owns them. A year earlier, OpenAI said it had “no specific plans to use TPUs at present.” [...] OpenAI has been moving in this direction for a while. It recently said it would offer its frontier models through Google Cloud. In June, it announced its first custom chip, and a current job listing asks for “significant experience optimizing real workloads on TPUs for training or inference.”

A buyer this large wants a second supplier because it gains leverage on price, protection against supply shortages, and software that is not tied to a single vendor. [...] OpenAI has spent more on NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) graphics processors than almost any other company, and it now plans to buy Google’s own AI chips, according to The Information. The report came out the night of October 27, 2026. It cites one person familiar with the matter and mentions Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs), custom chips built for AI work.

month.summary: Anthropic isn't the only one Nvidia should be worried about. OpenAI currently has a job listing for a software engineer to optimize its models for TPUs, and The Information reported Tuesday that OpenA...
highlights: Anthropic isn't the only one Nvidia should be worried about. OpenAI currently has a job listing for a software engineer to optimize its models for TPUs, and The Information reported Tuesday that OpenAI plans to buy TPUs from Google.

Meanwhile, several analysts have predicted Google's TPU business is about to explode as more companies hedge their bets with a multichip strategy — providing an opening for Google and others to further move onto Nvidia's turf. [...] In its IPO paperwork filed this week, Anthropic said it planned to spend $114.5 billion on Google compute between April 2026 and July 2033. While it didn't say how much of that would be going to TPUs specifically, it did estimate spending between $125 billion and $150 billion for TPU capacity from Google and other providers.
In the same filing, Anthropic said it's also using Amazon's Trainium chips and AMD's GPUs, in addition to chips from Nvidia and Google.

month.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPU chips, report says
month.summary: Last week, OpenAI announced a partnership placing its frontier models and the Codex coding agent inside Model Garden, Google Cloud’s AI catalog, where customers will pay through Google Cloud Marketpla...
highlights: Last week, OpenAI announced a partnership placing its frontier models and the Codex coding agent inside Model Garden, Google Cloud’s AI catalog, where customers will pay through Google Cloud Marketplace. Three of those models, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, entered private preview for select enterprise clients on Oct. 21, according to Google Cloud. [...] Broadcom CEO Hock Tan called the chip “just the beginning of a multi-generation roadmap.” Nothing in the TPU report explained how a Google purchase would fit alongside the Jalapeño program.

Unanswered questions include the TPU generation involved, the size of any order and the planned workload, training or serving. Anthropic, an OpenAI competitor, already buys TPUs, and its agreements have helped push up demand for Google’s chips. [...] Thomas Kurian, who runs Google Cloud, said the company wants customers to have “a broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI.” A TPU purchase would give Google a second role, as a hardware vendor to the lab whose models it now offers to cloud buyers.
Custom silicon is another track for OpenAI. On June 24, it unveiled Jalapeño, its first in-house AI accelerator, developed with Broadcom and slated for initial deployment before 2026 ends.
